newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees no WTO problems over new auto package.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees no WTO problems over new auto package.

text.p: Brazil does not expect to face any challenge from the World Trade Organization to its decision to offer tax and import tariff incentives to auto manufacturers who invest in the country's poor north, an official said.

"We do not see any difficulties arising from these measures but we are willing to talk should there be any doubts," Franciso Alvarez, executive secretary of the government's Foreign Trade Council, told reporters.

Earlier Thursday, Brazil published a presidential decree exempting automakers in Brazil's north, northeast and center-west regions from tax on company profits and from import tariffs and value-added tax on machinery and equipment among other benefits.
The decree has drawn criticism from Argentina which fears it will lure auto investments to Brazil.
Alvarez said the companies seeking to take advantage of the incentives had until March 31, 1997, to announce their investments.
The official mentioned Asia Motors, Hyundai and Italian motorcycle producer Biaggi as companies which had expressed interest in investing in the regions as a result of the incentives.
Alvarez said Brazil would have until July to formally inform the WTO of its decision to implement its "regional policy."

Several countries have challenged in the WTO another set of Brazilian incentives that seek to encourage auto investment by halving a 70 percent import tariff for firms who manufacture locally and who observe a 60 percent national content rule.
